newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA ANNOUNCES STEEL PLANT TRAINING PLAN.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA ANNOUNCES STEEL PLANT TRAINING PLAN.

text.p: South African Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka on Monday announced a four million rand project to train about 3,000 people for jobs linked to the Saldanha Steel project on the Atlantic west coast.
Mlambo-Ngcuka said the state-financed Industrial Development Corporation and foreign donors would fund the 12-month West Coast Training Initiative based in a factory building near Saldanha Bay.
"The training is being geared towards upgrading and promoting workers from an unskilled to a semi-skilled level," she said.
Selected men and women from the economically depressed Saldanha area would be trained in mechanical, civil and electrical engineering and hotel and restaurant skills.

The Saldanha steel mill, which is being built close to a shipping terminal and at the end of a rail line from the Sishen iron ore fields, is South Africa's biggest post-apartheid industrial investment.
